published_source: Published article, Appendix Table C.3, column (1) General Access, row Average Credit Score (appendix printed in the article, papers/mnsc/mnsc.2025.02515.pdf; text in data/text/mnsc/mnsc.2025.02515.txt): -0.611*** (0.207). published_coef/published_se are the printed digits. The authors' code.R re-run on the package data (did 2.5.1, att_gt dr, notyettreated, varying base, weights num_individs_2015, cluster county, bstrap = FALSE; aggte simple, min_e = -8, max_e = 16) gives -0.6108937003 (analytic SE 0.204727), stored in authors_rerun_coef; did 2.1.2 (the authors' pin, R 4.3.2) gives the same value to 7 significant digits. Checked Nov 4 2026 (appx_nov4/verify_appx_authors.R).
notes: PRINTED-APPENDIX SPECIFICATION (Nov 4, 2026): outside the main-text sample (PROTOCOL 5b ruling (r)); for the appendix-inclusive sensitivity analysis. General Access design (gvar first_treat_time), CEM-matched sample of Appendix Table C.3 column (1) and Figures C.1-C.2 (General Access panels). Matching: MatchIt::matchit(treated ~ young_men + total_population + low_income + median_income + education + unemployment, method = 'cem', k2k = TRUE, ratio = 1) on general_access_county_matching_info.csv (2015-2017 county averages), code.R lines 789-812. The matched counties enter ONLY as a sample restriction: code.R keeps the rows of final-reg-data.csv whose numeric_state_county is in match.data()'s county list and re-runs generate_results() with the usual num_individs_2015 weights; MatchIt's matching weights (all 1 under k2k 1:1) are never used, so this is a 1:1 matched sample (PROTOCOL 5b: eligible), not a matching estimator. sample_filter lists the 1,398 matched counties (699 treated, 699 never-treated; article Appendix C.1: 'matching leaves us with 699 treated counties (out of 1,837) and 699 control counties'), reproduced with MatchIt 4.7.2 on the shipped file order (authors pin 4.7.0; the 4.7.1-4.7.2 changes do not touch CEM; the matched set reproduces all 12 printed matched-sample entries of Appendix Table C.1, differences and SEs, to 4 decimals; appx_nov4/check_cem_balance.log). The k2k pairing depends on row order (a shuffled file selects other counties), so the list is fixed in the spec. Sample: 1,398 counties, quarters 1-30, 41,940 rows, balanced; 13 adoption cohorts (quarters 10,11,12,15,16,17,18,20,21,23,24,27,29); 699 never-treated counties (50.0% of rows); no always-treated counties. Authors report Callaway-Sant'Anna with the main-text settings (code.R generate_results(), lines 277-364: did::att_gt, control_group = 'notyettreated', est_method = 'dr', base_period = 'varying', allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE, xformla = ~1, weightsname = 'num_individs_2015', clustervars = county, bstrap = TRUE without a seed; aggte(type = 'simple' or 'dynamic', min_e = -8, max_e = 16)). No TWFE regression exists in the package; the TWFE counterpart is D = 1[gvar > 0 & time >= gvar] with county FE + quarter FE, weights num_individs_2015, clustered by county. Treatment never switches off (defined from a unit-constant timing variable). Outcome levels were additively transformed by the authors to hide actual levels (README); county IDs anonymized; underlying UC Consumer Credit Panel is restricted. Project member Davide Proserpio is a coauthor (PROTOCOL Section 6). y_sd_* are computed on the non-missing rows of the sample before drop_e_above, as in the main-text template.
